title: Morning Briefing — November 7, 2026
subtitle: 8 made-up stories for layout and publishing tests.
intro: This is a sandbox edition generated by scripts/sandbox.mjs. Outlets, towns and people are fictional, links go to example.com, and photos are random placeholders.

stories.headline: Tech employer to add 600 jobs at new North Ridge campus
stories.summary: Cloud software company Lattice & Pine says it will build a regional campus in North Ridge and hire 600 people over three years. The state approved $12 million in performance-based tax credits tied to the hiring.

stories.headline: School district pilots four-day week at six rural schools
stories.summary: Six rural schools in the Redwater district will move to a four-day week starting in January as part of a two-year pilot. District leaders say the change could help recruit teachers; some parents worry about child care on Fridays.

stories.headline: Regional grocer Copper Basket to open three new stores
stories.summary: Copper Basket, a family-owned grocery chain, says it will open stores in Aspen Flats, Redwater and North Ridge over the next 18 months. The company plans to hire about 400 people and expand its locally sourced produce program.

stories.headline: Early-season storm to drop up to a foot of snow on the high country
stories.summary: Forecasters expect a fast-moving storm to bring 6 to 12 inches of snow above 9,000 feet by Tuesday morning. Lower elevations should see a cold rain turning to light snow overnight, with slick commutes likely along the mountain corridor.

image.caption: random sample photo used for layout testing.

stories.headline: Brewery wins national gold medal for its winter ale
stories.summary: High Desert Brewing took gold at a national beer competition for its spiced winter ale. The small brewery says it will double production of the seasonal beer this year.

stories.headline: Volunteers plant 5,000 trees along restored creek
stories.summary: About 600 volunteers planted willows and cottonwoods along a two-mile stretch of Silver Creek that was straightened decades ago. The restoration aims to cool the water and bring back native trout.

image.caption: placeholder image for a made-up story.

stories.headline: Peach growers report record harvest despite late frost
stories.summary: Western-slope orchards shipped a record 1.2 million boxes of peaches this season, growers say, after a late-April frost spared most high-elevation trees. Prices to farmers were up slightly from last year.

image.alt: Placeholder photo for the story “Peach growers report record harvest despite late frost”
image.caption: stock placeholder, not related to the story.

stories.headline: Reservoir levels climb to highest point in five years
stories.summary: Thanks to a wet spring and a cool summer, Blue Mesa-area reservoirs are at 87 percent of capacity, the highest level since 2021. Water managers caution that a single good year does not end the long-term drought.
